correctness.rationale: Every finite class signature has an explicit characteristic formula of the stated modal depth. Equality of entire signature vectors is a color-preserving bisimulation, proved by recursively matching a successor through blocks and inheriting higher ancestor signatures. The rooted-tree rigidity equivalence follows by induction on child subtree isomorphism types. The counting recurrence is the classical distinguishing-tree recurrence on these rigid colorings, with a separate binary three-type construction proving the sharp H-1 depth. Exhaustive regular/nonuniform finite models, direct modal Boolean closures, and height-seven sharpness tests corroborate the proof; all hypotheses and uniformity restrictions are stated.

value.rationale: The problem asks exactly which finite hierarchical epistemic states one can isolate with propositional valuations in ordinary modal logic. The theorem gives a complete quotient computation for all finite nested hierarchies, a rigidity criterion for full generation, a sharp modal-depth cutoff independent of world count, and a bounded-generator family of arbitrarily large finite frames. These structural facts are not merely numeric substitutions into Cheng’s recursion.
